claims: Turning 60 before 30 June moves the rate from 32% to 17%.
whys: Correct today, but the 60 is typed into the text while the same file imports PRESERVATION_AGE. The caption at line 126 ('Preservation age is 60 for anyone born after 30 June 1964') also types the age instead of using the constant.

claims: A TOIL day is 'often shown as its own line with a running balance' on your payslip.
When untaken TOIL is paid out, it must be paid at the overtime rate that applied when you worked it (the FAQ at time-in-lieu-faqs.ts lines 25 and 29 says the same).
whys: This is a claim about how often payslips show TOIL, and the page gives no source for it. Payslip rules (Fair Work Regulations reg 3.46) do not require a TOIL balance line. Either cite a source or reword it as a check the reader can make.

lib/constants/time-in-lieu.ts lines 23-25 and the SCHADS rule note (line 172) say SCHADS pays untaken TOIL 'based on the rates of pay applying at the time payment is made' (cl 28.2(e)-(f),(j)). Under SCHADS, the rate used is the one in force at payout, not the one in force when the overtime was worked. The blanket statement does not hold for SCHADS. The constants header (line 27-30, 'Common to all eight') contradicts its own SCHADS note.
constants: lib/constants/time-in-lieu.ts TOIL_AWARD_RULES (SCHADS note) and header comment
reviewerNotes: Writer's question, still open: 'often shown as its own line with a running balance' is a population claim about payslips with no source given. It is in the original text and the writer did not change it.
